exposure: Practitioner type (certified nurse-midwife, family medicine physician)
cohort: The study included 40,589 nulliparous patients with term, singleton, vertex births at 68 hospitals in a statewide obstetric quality collaborative between January 2020 and June 2021.
finding: Postpartum opioid prescribing after birth shows high variation largely driven by practitioner- and hospital-level factors.
mod_finding: Cesarean birth was the strongest patient-level predictor of receiving a postpartum opioid prescription (aOR 899.1).
